basics.name: Adi Banerjee
basics.label: Software Engineer
basics.summary: Software engineer at Amazon in Seattle building agentic systems for vendor operations: an MCP server backed by DuckDB over S3 Parquet, a graph-based documentation-drift detector on Bedrock, and a real-time sourcing-explainability agent over a 30M-document OpenSearch index.

work.name: Amazon
highlights: Built agentic capabilities for dropship vendors to diagnose delivery performance drops and warehouse suspensions through Amazon's vendor-facing AI assistant: an MCP server and skills backed by DuckDB over S3 Parquet, built spec-first with OpenSpec, evaluated with Langfuse traces and LLM judges, and authorized per user by task-based role.

Proposed and built a documentation-drift detector that models a wiki corpus as a Neptune graph and uses a Rust Lambda on Bedrock to find stale pages and generate reviewable edits. A topic-based diff algorithm feeds the model 200 tokens of graph topics per query instead of 50K tokens of page content, analyzing 30+ pages in under 5s from a 48ms cold start.

Designed the ingestion layer and co-built a sourcing-explainability agent that streams buying-decision changes from 3 upstream systems through Kinesis and Lambda into OpenSearch (30M documents): a 100ms lookup replaces multi-hop API resolution, with a 7.5s p95 time to first token against a 20s requirement and 85s end-to-end answers from a 198s p95 baseline.

Co-designed and led launch of embedded QuickSight dashboards in Vendor Central across 5 marketplaces (React, Java, CDK), retiring a 7-service legacy analytics stack so analysts publish new metrics without engineering work.

Amazon SCOT hackathons: Spark 2025 winner (multi-agent tech-debt profiler on LangGraph, 1000+ teams), OSS AI 2026 runner-up for Technical Excellence (the drift detector, 18,800+ lines across 3 packages shipped to beta in 2.5 days), Spark 2026 Evaluation & Verification Award.

work.name: Amazon
highlights: Led a suspension system overhaul with EventBridge batch processing and DynamoDB distributed rate limiting: execution from 2 days to 5 min, throughput from 1 to 200 requests/min.
Tech lead across 3 teams on a network optimization workflow affecting 230MM+ configs.

Migrated 26 vendor email use cases across 12 services off a 10-year-old Tier-1 notification service to SES and an internal platform, using 11 service-level feature flags on a graduated rollout, with a 0% error rate since launch.

work.name: University of Arizona
highlights: Built deep RL transformer models for math OCR with a 6% gain over SOTA, and rewrote the MathML parser in Rust (Nom).

projects.name: Whisper
projects.summary: Shared daily safe-word service with Google OAuth, timezone-aware rotation, JNI-based Rust word generation, Bucket4j rate limiting, Prometheus metrics, and a Helm chart for Kubernetes deployment.

projects.name: dups
projects.summary: Concurrent duplicate file finder with a two-pass hashing strategy (4KB partial hash for files over 1MB, full SHA-256 for confirmed candidates), channel-based worker pool, interactive per-group deletion, and cross-platform builds via goreleaser.

projects.name: Hindsight
projects.summary: Keyless backtest visualizer for equity trading strategies with real-time portfolio charting, trade annotation, and drawdown analysis. Deployed on Vercel with GitHub Actions CI.

projects.name: TaylorGPT
projects.summary: Designed a 1.4M parameter character-level transformer decoder model to generate Taylor Swift lyrics from scratch using PyTorch. Built custom masking, multi-head attention, transformer blocks, and enabled multi-GPU training.

projects.name: Start Journey
projects.summary: Designed a full-stack stable diffusion-based image generator with PyTorch, CUDA, HuggingFace, and FastAPI for the backend and React in TypeScript for the frontend. Enabled scalable image generation and user-friendly web interface.
highlights: Python, PyTorch, HuggingFace, CUDA, FastAPI, React
